# Tidewater incident log 2025

A summary of the incidents reported to the marine superintendent in 2025.
Each entry gives the date, the vessel, what happened and what was done about
it. Drills are recorded in the crew handbook's drill log, not here.

## January to March

On 14 January, MV Osprey's port water-jet intake picked up a length of
fishing net off Pellin Island. The vessel completed the crossing on the
starboard jet at reduced speed, and a diver cleared the intake at the
Harlow berth that evening. No damage was found. On 2 February, a vehicle
on MV Kestrel's vehicle deck rolled forward about half a metre during
loading because its handbrake had not been set; it touched no other
vehicle, and deckhands now chock every vehicle on the ramp side before the
bow door closes. On 27 March, MV Heron arrived for its winter charter with
an expired liferaft certificate; the charter start was delayed by two days
while the liferafts were serviced.

## April to June

On 9 April, a passenger on MV Kestrel slipped on the wet stairs to the
upper deck and sprained an ankle; anti-slip strips were added to every
external staircase on both vessels by the end of the month. On 21 May,
MV Osprey's number 3 engine shut down on high coolant temperature on the
Dunmere approach; the vessel berthed on three engines and the engine was
exchanged overnight. On 30 June, the Pellin Island berth's pontoon lost a
mooring chain in a storm, and sailings to Pellin were suspended for two
days until the chain was replaced.

## July to September

On 12 July, a dog broke free of its owner's lead on MV Osprey's aft deck
and was recovered by a deckhand; the pet rules were reprinted on the aft
deck notices. On 18 August, MV Kestrel touched bottom leaving Harlow at an
unusually low spring tide; a diver inspection found no damage and the
master's standing orders now forbid departures from Harlow within 40
minutes of low water on spring tides. On 23 September, a wheelchair user's
booking at Harlow was not passed to terminal staff, and the passenger
waited 25 minutes for assistance at Gangway A before being moved to
Gangway B; the booking app now alerts the terminal as soon as assistance is
requested.

## October to December

On 5 October, MV Kestrel's bow thruster failed during berthing at Dunmere
in a crosswind, and the vessel berthed with tug assistance; the thruster
motor was replaced at the November dry-dock. On 19 November, a fuel
delivery at Harlow was found to contain water; bunkering was stopped and
the delivery was rejected, and both vessels sailed on their existing fuel
within the reserve rules. On 11 December, a passenger's medical oxygen
cylinder was found undeclared at the Harlow terminal and held there until
the passenger returned.
